page: Microsoft Azure E48ns_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server from the Env6 family built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Hardware features include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache, along with Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instructions. System memory is configured at 384.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided.

Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong computational and memory performance. The instance achieved top-quartile results in PassMark CPU testing (55,897.62) and PassMark database operations (22,537.9), alongside strong extended instruction and encryption metrics. Large-block uncached memory throughput scored within the top 25% of evaluated systems, registering 222.79 GB/sec for read operations and 94.78 GB/sec for write operations. Data processing capabilities are further evidenced by single-threaded gzip compression at 31.39 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 265.69 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reached 73.77 GB/sec, while small-model LLM prompt processing attained 3,329.74 tokens per second.

From an architectural perspective, the E48ns_v6 maximizes memory density and memory bandwidth efficiency for enterprise scale. Because local instance storage is absent, workloads requiring persistence must integrate remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage over the network. The instance offers strong qualitative resource value for applications requiring high RAM-to-vCPU ratios without paying overhead for unused local disks or GPU silicon. Primary workload targets include in-memory databases, large transactional database systems, memory-bound caching layers, ETL pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving environments.

Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 384.0 GB of dedicated system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB-per-vCPU ratio. It incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 capabilities alongside a generous 260 MB L3 cache. In benchmark evaluations, the E48ns_v6 demonstrates top-quartile results across PassMark CPU and database operation metrics, backed by strong uncached memory bandwidth measuring 222.79 GB/sec read and 94.78 GB/sec write. Because this instance includes no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, persistent data management relies exclusively on external network-attached volumes such as Premium Storage.
